prompt: It is January 2, 2019. I would like to outperform the S&P 500 over the next five years. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy? Answer as of that date.
reply:
# Ten Stocks to Outperform the S&P 500, as of January 2, 2019

I can't fully put myself in January 2019, because I know what happened from 2019 through 2024. Any list I write now is shaped by that hindsight, even when I try to avoid it. So below is a list a reasonable analyst could have defended with what was known on that date, followed by how it actually turned out.

## The picks, with the reasoning available at the time

The fourth-quarter 2018 selloff (the S&P fell nearly 20% from its peak) left many high-quality companies at reasonable valuations. The idea is to buy durable leaders at those prices, weight them equally, and hold for five years.

| # | Stock | Case as of Jan 2, 2019 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Microsoft (MSFT)** | Azure grew 76% last quarter, and the shift of Office to subscriptions makes revenue recurring. It just became the world's most valuable company. |
| 2 | **Apple (AAPL)** | About 13x earnings, heavy buybacks and a growing services business. It cut its revenue guidance after the close today, so expect a cheaper entry point tomorrow. |
| 3 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Search and YouTube dominate digital advertising, and the company holds over $100B in net cash. The market gives little value to its cloud business or Waymo. |
| 4 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | AWS alone is a roughly $27B-a-year business, advertising is growing quickly, and the stock is down about 25% from its September high. |
| 5 | **Visa (V)** | It profits from the long global shift from cash to cards, with very high margins and little credit risk. |
| 6 | **UnitedHealth (UNH)** | The largest US health insurer, and its Optum services arm is growing faster than insurance. It has a long record of steady growth. |
| 7 | **JPMorgan Chase (JPM)** | The best-run large bank, earning record profits at about 10x earnings. |
| 8 | **Boeing (BA)** | A record backlog of about 5,900 airplanes, a planned ramp-up in 737 production and large buybacks. It is a consensus favorite. |
| 9 | **Disney (DIS)** | The Fox acquisition should close soon, and Disney+ launches in late 2019. Its content library is unmatched. |
| 10 | **Nvidia (NVDA)** | A contrarian pick. The stock is down about 55% since October because of a gaming inventory glut left over from crypto mining. Its long-term drivers are data centers and AI. |

## How it actually turned out

These are approximate price returns from January 2, 2019 to the end of 2023, adjusted for splits and excluding dividends.

| Stock | Return |
|---|---|
| Nvidia | ~+1,350% |
| Apple | ~+390% |
| Microsoft | ~+270% |
| Alphabet | ~+165% |
| UnitedHealth | ~+115% |
| Amazon | ~+95% |
| Visa | ~+95% |
| JPMorgan | ~+70% |
| Disney | ~−17% |
| Boeing | ~−20% |
| **S&P 500** | **~+90% (~+107% with dividends)** |

Weighted equally, the portfolio returned roughly +250%. Even without Nvidia, it would have returned about +130%, well ahead of the index.

## Why you shouldn't read too much into this

- **Hindsight is doing a lot of the work.** Nvidia's inclusion is the most obvious case. In January 2019 it was a falling stock with an uncertain recovery, and I picked it partly because I know what came next.
- **The consensus favorites of the time mostly failed.** Boeing faced the 737 MAX groundings starting in March 2019 and then COVID. Disney ran into streaming losses. Both were among the most widely recommended stocks in early 2019.
- **Picking stocks usually loses to the index.** S&P's SPIVA reports found that roughly three-quarters or more of US large-cap funds trailed the S&P 500 over the five years ending in 2023. Beating the index was much harder in real time than this table suggests.

If you're investing today (September 2026), a low-cost S&P 500 index fund is the benchmark to beat, and it's hard to beat reliably.
